record.paper_title: OPEN QUESTIONS FOR OPERATORS RELATED TO RECTANGULAR CATALAN COMBINATORICS
record.context_brief: Schur positivity of renormalized Schur-seed operators
record.original_question: For a partition μ of d and coprime integers a,b ≥ 1, let Θ_{a,b}: Λ → E be the elliptic-Hall-algebra monomorphism used in the paper, and let s^{(a,b)}_μ(x;q,t) := Θ_{a,b}(s_μ)(1). Writing ι(μ) = Σ_{i=1}^{ℓ(μ)} χ(μ_i - i), is the renormalized symmetric function (-qt)^(-ι(μ)) s^{(a,b)}_μ(x;q,t) always Schur-positive, meaning that its Schur expansion has coefficients in N[q,t]? If yes, can this positivity be explained by exhibiting a bigraded S_n-subrepresentation of the generalized diagonal harmonics module whose bigraded Frobenius characteristic is this expression?

evidence.quote: Because of ties with representation theory, we are interested in functions fd such that the application of the operators Θa,b(fd) to the constant symmetric function 1 gives Schur-positive symmetric function, for any coprime a, b ≥ 1. When this is so, we say that fd gives rise to Schur-positive operators, and denote by f(a,b)d (x; q, t) the symmetric function Θa,b(fd)(1).
the renormalized Schur functions (−qt)−ι(µ) sµ(x) where, for an integer partition µ of d, we set ι(µ) := Σℓ(µ)i=1 χ(µ(i) − i);

Question.1. Can we prove that 0 ⪯s (−qt)−ι(µ) s(a,b)µ (x, q, t), for all partition µ of d, and all coprime a, b ≥ 1? Can we explain this in terms of bigraded subrepresentations of the Sn-module of generalized diagonal harmonics?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Lambda$ denote the ring of symmetric functions in variables $x = (x_1, x_2, \ldots)$ over the field $\mathbb{Q}(q,t)$, with Schur basis $\{s_\mu\}$ indexed by integer partitions. Let $\mathcal{E}$ denote the elliptic Hall algebra (acting on $\Lambda$ via the Schiffmann–Vasserot action / Macdonald-eigenoperators). For each pair of coprime positive integers $(a,b)$, there is a known algebra monomorphism
$$\Theta_{a,b}\colon \Lambda \longrightarrow \mathcal{E}$$
sending the power-sum $p_d$ (for $d = \gcd$-scaled appropriately) to a distinguished generator $D_{a,b}$ of $\mathcal{E}$ along the slope-$b/a$ ray. For a partition $\mu \vdash d$, define
$$s^{(a,b)}_\mu(x;q,t) := \Theta_{a,b}(s_\mu)\cdot 1 \in \Lambda_{\mathbb{Q}(q,t)},$$
where $\Theta_{a,b}(s_\mu)$ is applied to the constant symmetric function $1$.

For an integer $k$, set $\chi(k) := 1$ if $k \geq 0$ and $\chi(k) := 0$ otherwise, and for a partition $\mu = (\mu_1 \geq \mu_2 \geq \cdots \geq \mu_{\ell(\mu)} > 0)$ define
$$\iota(\mu) := \sum_{i=1}^{\ell(\mu)} \chi(\mu_i - i).$$

A symmetric function $f(x;q,t) \in \Lambda_{\mathbb{Q}(q,t)}$ is called Schur-positive (written $0 \preceq_s f$) if its expansion in the Schur basis has all coefficients in $\mathbb{N}[q,t]$.

(a) Prove or disprove: for every pair of coprime integers $a,b \geq 1$ and every partition $\mu$,
$$(-qt)^{-\iota(\mu)}\, s^{(a,b)}_\mu(x;q,t)$$
is Schur-positive.

(b) If (a) holds, exhibit a bigraded $S_n$-subrepresentation of the generalized $(a,b)$-diagonal harmonics module whose bigraded Frobenius characteristic equals $(-qt)^{-\iota(\mu)} s^{(a,b)}_\mu(x;q,t)$, thereby giving a representation-theoretic explanation of the Schur positivity.
artifact.category_tag: Schur positivity and elliptic Hall algebra
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not return a definitive resolution of this Schur-positivity conjecture for the renormalized symmetric functions $(-qt)^{-\iota(\mu)} s^{(a,b)}_\mu(x;q,t)$ obtained from the elliptic Hall algebra monomorphism. Related conjectures of Bergeron–Garsia–Sergel–Xin in this circle (notably the rectangular shuffle/compositional shuffle theorem) have been proved by Mellit, but the specific Schur-positivity question for all partitions $\mu$ and all coprime $(a,b)$, together with its representation-theoretic interpretation in generalized diagonal harmonics, does not appear to have a published proof or counterexample, so the status is best classified as unknown/open.
